current_events: Several people are killed and at least 10 others are injured after the Russian corvette Merkury is struck by a Ukrainian naval drone attack while docked at the port of Benghazi, Libya. The Merkury later capsizes and sinks
The M/V Angara, a Russian-flagged cargo ship, is also struck by naval drones off the coast of Benghazi in the Mediterranean Sea
Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukrainian attacks on the Russian shadow fleet

The Catholic World Report notes that at least 140 people were killed by Allied Democratic Forces and Islamic State Central Africa Province attacks targeting Christians in the Democratic Republic of the Congo provinces of North Kivu and Ituri over the course of two weeks earlier in November
Allied Democratic Forces insurgency

Twenty-four people, including seven children, are killed in an attack by the armed wing of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-in-Opposition in Tonj East County, Warrap State, South Sudan. Four attackers are also killed
Two people are killed and thirteen others are abducted in two separate bandit attacks in Magaji and Maru, Zamfara State, Nigeria
The 63rd Golden Horse Awards take place in Taipei, Taiwan, with the Hong Kong film We Are Born Good winning Best Narrative Feature

Several garment factories in Gazipur, Bangladesh declare holidays amid ongoing minimum wage protests, as clashes erupt between workers and police along the Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway, with workers throwing bricks and police firing tear gas and stun grenades while Special Response Battalion, Ansar, BGB, and Industrial Police personnel deploy to the area

Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, stepping up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones using drones and police body cameras
2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
At least twelve people are killed and 23 others are injured in two separate road accidents in Rajasthan, India
A severe thunderstorm kills five people and injures more than 250 others in Tupanciretã, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
Three people are killed in a house fire in Trzcianka, Poland
Carbon monoxide poisoning from a suspected heater malfunction during Sunday mass at a church in Bad Grönenbach, Bavaria, Germany, leaves 56 people injured

The 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, concludes without a final agreement after countries failed to reach consensus on fossil fuel policies. It is the longest climate summit on record
2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference

Democratic Republic of the Congo president Félix Tshisekedi and Kenyan president William Ruto agree to restore full diplomatic relations after a summit in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, hosted by the country's president Denis Sassou Nguesso and mediated by Togolese former president Faure Gnassingbé
Democratic Republic of the Congo–Kenya relations

The Co-op Live arena in Manchester, England, is evacuated of around 12000 attendees after an unknown substance is dispersed during a Don Toliver concert, initially believed to be tear gas, causing respiratory distress to multiple concertgoers

South Korean education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigns following criticism of the government's response to artificial intelligence-assisted cheating concerns surrounding the College Scholastic Ability Test. President Lee Jae Myung accepts Choi's resignation
In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev 6–2, 7–6(9–7) in the final to win his first singles title at the 2026 ATP Finals

In motorcycle racing, Spanish rider Marc Márquez of Ducati Corse secures his eighth MotoGP World Championship after finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix, equalling Giacomo Agostini's record for the most premier-class motorcycle racing world titles
